# Page spec reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run page-spec-docs` from the kit catalogues and settings. Do not edit by hand. -->

A page spec is a compact, nested JSON description of a page (`.page.json`). Import one with **File → Import page spec…**, by dropping the file on the editor, or by pasting the JSON. Each page becomes a new frame. **Copy as page spec** on a frame gives you the same format back, so a frame can go through a chat and return.

Several pages: put them in a list, `{ "format": "mockup-page-spec", "version": 1, "pages": [ { "name": "Home", "kit": "nsw", "page": [ … ] }, … ] }`. Each page may set `name`, `kit`, `device` (iphone, android, tablet, desktop), `width` (240 to 3000), `settings` and `page`.

The importer is forgiving and reports what it did: an unknown component becomes a labelled placeholder, an unknown variant becomes the default, unknown text keys, options and settings are dropped, and an item in a place the rules do not allow is moved to the nearest valid place.

## Instruction for Claude

Paste this, then the reference for the kit you need (File → Copy page spec instructions copies both), with your screenshot:

```text
Recreate the attached screenshot as a page spec for the NSW Mockup Builder.

1. Choose the kit and set "kit": "nsw" for NSW Government sites, "sharepoint" for SharePoint or Microsoft 365 pages.
2. Use only the components, variants, text keys, options and settings listed in that kit's reference below. Use the closest variant when nothing matches exactly.
3. Copy all visible text exactly. Do not invent content you cannot see.
4. For anything with no match (a map, a chart you cannot express, a custom widget), add `{ "component": "<what it is>" }` with a name that is not in the list. The app turns it into a clearly labelled placeholder.
5. Follow the section, row and column shapes and the rules below, and keep the order of the page.
6. Output only the JSON: one object with "format": "mockup-page-spec" and "version": 1. No explanation, no code fences.
```

## NSW Design System (`"kit": "nsw"`)

### Shapes

- **Top level** (`page`): a list of items. Each is either a component, or a section.
- **Component**: `{ "component": "card", "variant": "default", "text": { "title": "…" }, "props": { … }, "hide": ["image"] }`. A full-width component (masthead, header, main navigation, footer, hero banner, …) sits directly in `page`. Any other component put directly in `page` is wrapped in a section for you.
- **Section**: `{ "section": { "background": "off-white", "padding": "half", "flush": true }, "blocks": [ … ] }`. `blocks` holds components (stacked in one column) and rows.
- **Row**: `{ "row": [8, 4], "columns": [ [component, …], [component, …] ] }`. `row` has one width per column, out of 12 from the medium breakpoint up (phones stack). A width can also be an object by breakpoint: `{ "base": 12, "md": 6, "lg": 4 }`. At most 6 columns.
- **Section settings**: `background` (white, off-white, brand-light, brand-dark, brand-supplementary, grey-01, grey-02, grey-03, grey-04, black), `padding` (default, half, none), `flush` (true: edge to edge).

### Rules

- Components that span the whole page cannot be inside a section or a column; they are moved to just after it.
- Sections cannot be nested, and rows must be inside a section.
- A row has at most 6 columns.

### Frame settings (`settings`)

_None._

**Section settings**

| Key | Values | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `background` | white \| off-white \| brand-light \| brand-dark \| brand-supplementary \| grey-01 \| grey-02 \| grey-03 \| grey-04 \| black | `white` | Background: Section background |
| `padding` | default \| half \| none | `default` | Padding: Section padding |

**Container settings**

| Key | Values | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flush` | true \| false | `false` | Container: Edge to edge (no side padding) |

### Worked example

```json
{
  "format": "mockup-page-spec",
  "version": 1,
  "kit": "nsw",
  "name": "Home",
  "device": "desktop",
  "settings": {},
  "page": [
    {
      "component": "masthead",
      "variant": "dark"
    },
    {
      "component": "header",
      "variant": "default",
      "text": {
        "title": "Service NSW",
        "description": "Everyday services"
      }
    },
    {
      "component": "main-nav",
      "variant": "default"
    },
    {
      "section": {
        "background": "off-white"
      },
      "blocks": [
        {
          "component": "heading",
          "variant": "h1",
          "text": {
            "text": "Find a service"
          }
        },
        {
          "row": [
            6,
            6
          ],
          "columns": [
            [
              {
                "component": "card",
                "variant": "default",
                "text": {
                  "title": "Apply",
                  "copy": "Apply online in minutes."
                }
              }
            ],
            [
              {
                "component": "button",
                "variant": "dark",
                "text": {
                  "label": "Get started"
                }
              }
            ]
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "component": "footer",
      "variant": "dark"
    }
  ]
}
```

## SharePoint (out of the box) (`"kit": "sharepoint"`)

### Shapes

- **Top level** (`page`): a list of sections. A web part put directly in `page` is wrapped in a one-column section for you.
- **Section**: `{ "section": { "layout": "two-columns", "background": "soft" }, "columns": [ [webpart, …], [webpart, …] ] }`. One list per column.
- **Layouts** (`section.layout`): `one-column`, `two-columns`, `three-columns`, `one-third-left` (2 columns), `one-third-right` (2 columns), `full-width` (1), `vertical` (1), `flexible` (1). Extra columns are merged into the last; missing ones are left empty.
- **Web part**: `{ "component": "sp-news", "variant": "list", "text": { … }, "props": { … }, "hide": [ … ] }`.
- **Frame settings** (`settings`, top of the file): the site (communication or team), suite bar, header, navigation, footer and page title area. See the settings table below. Menus and footer links are lists: `"navItems": [ { "label": "Home" }, { "label": "News", "children": [ { "label": "Latest" } ] } ]`.

### Rules

- A full-width section needs a communication site.
- A page has at most one vertical section, and not together with a full-width section.
- A flexible section can only be added as a new section; it cannot be turned into another layout.
- A vertical section cannot be collapsible.
- Team sites have a left-hand menu and no footer.
- Where a rule is broken, the section becomes a one-column section (or the setting is left out), and the import report says so.

| `navVisible` | true \| false | `true` | Navigation: Show navigation |

| `collapseIcon` | left \| right | `left` | Collapsible: Expand and collapse icon |
| `collapsedByDefault` | true \| false | `false` | Collapsible: Collapsed when the page opens |
